<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin="par152" />{{GHGheb|text=לֹא... מִפְּנֵי־כֹל}} and turneth ''not'' away ''for any''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=32|verse=15}}; but cf. also the inverted order, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=12|verse=16}} {{GHGheb|text=כָּל־מְלָאכָה לֹא־יֵֽעָשֶׂה|translate=no manner of work shall be done}}; 12:43, 15:26, 22:21, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=16|verse=17}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=33|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dn|chapter=11|verse=37}}. The meaning is different when {{GHGheb|text=כֹּל}} by being determinate is used in the sense of ''whole'', e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=23|verse=13}} {{GHGheb|text=כֻּלּוֹ לֹא תִרְאֶה|translate=thou shalt not see them all}}, but only a part.

Analogous to {{GHGheb|text=לֹא... כֹּל}} is the use of {{GHGheb|text=אִישׁ... לֹא}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=23|verse=6}}, &c., in verbal-clauses in the sense of ''no one at all, not a single one''. On {{GHGheb|text=אֵין־כֹּל|translate=nothing at all}}, see under ''p''.

{{GHGmargin-letter|152|c}}
Rem. 1. The examples in which {{GHGheb|text=לֹא}} is used absolutely as a negative answer, equivalent to ''certainly not! no!'' must be regarded as extremely short verbal-clauses, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=19|verse=2}} ({{GHGheb|text=לֹא}} according to the context for {{GHGheb|text=לֹא נָסוּר}} &c.); 23:11, 42:10, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Hag|chapter=2|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=23|verse=6}}, sometimes with a following {{GHGheb|text=כִּי|translate=but}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=19|verse=2}} (see above); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=5|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=3|verse=22}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|152|d}}
2. The negation of ''noun''-clauses by {{GHGheb|text=לֹא}} (as opposed to the regular negation by {{GHGheb|text=אֵין}}) always includes a certain emphasis, since the force of the negation falls rather upon a particular word (cf. e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=36|verse=32}}), than upon the whole clause. In {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=3|verse=34}} {{GHGheb|text=יָדֶ֫יךָ לֹֽא־אֲסוּרוֹת|translate=thy hands}} were ''not bound'', a participle is thus specially negatived by {{GHGheb|text=לֹא}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=74|verse=9}}, where, however, {{GHGheb|text=לֹא}} is separated from the participle by {{GHGheb|text=אִתָּ֫נוּ}}, and {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=12|verse=3}}. As a rule, noun-clauses with a pronominal subject are thus negatived by {{GHGheb|text=לֹא}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=20|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=35|verse=23}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=4|verse=42}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=19|verse=4|hidebook=1}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=15|verse=29}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=21|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=4|verse=22}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=22|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=28|verse=14}}, parallel with {{GHGheb|text=אֵין}}; generally with {{GHGheb|text=לֹא}} before a substantival predicate, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=4|verse=10}} {{GHGheb|text=לֹא אִישׁ דְּבָרִים אָנֹ֫כִי|translate=I am not a man of words}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=5|verse=18}}.—Noun-clauses with a substantival subject, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=29|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=23|verse=19}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=22|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=44|verse=19|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Hag|chapter=1|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=22|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=9|verse=32}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=18|verse=17|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=21|verse=9|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=22|verse=16|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=36|verse=26|hidebook=1}} (with {{GHGheb|text=וְ}} of the apodosis); 41:2; in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=9|verse=33}} even {{GHGheb|text=לֹא יֵשׁ|translate=non est}} is used instead of {{GHGheb|text=אֵין}}.—In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=18|verse=5}} {{GHGheb|text=לֹא}} is used before an adjectival predicate; in {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=20|verse=26}} (where a preceding noun-clause is negatived by {{GHGheb|text=בִּלְתִּי}}) read {{GHGheb|text=לֹא טֹהָר}} with the LXX, for {{GHGheb|text=לֹא טָהוֹר}}. On {{GHGheb|text=לֹא}} for {{GHGheb|text=אֵין}} in circumstantial clauses to express attributive ideas, see ''u'' below.

{{GHGmargin-letter|152|e}}
3. As a rule {{GHGheb|text=לֹא}} stands immediately before the verb, but sometimes is separated from it (frequently to bring into special prominence another word which follows it); thus {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=22|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=10|verse=10}} before the object and verb; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=16|verse=29}} before the subject and verb; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=8|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=3|verse=34}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=49|verse=18}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=103|verse=10|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=13|verse=16}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=34|verse=23|hidebook=1}} before a complementary adjunct. In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=32|verse=5}} {{GHGheb|text=לֹא}} according to the accentuation even stands at the end of the clause (''they offend him not''); but undoubtedly {{GHGheb|text=לֹא בָנָיו}} are to be taken together.—On the position of {{GHGheb|text=לֹא}} with the infinitive absolute, see {{GHGpar|113|v}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|152|f}}
(''b'') {{GHGheb|text=אַל־}} is used like μή and ''ne'' to express a ''subjective'' and ''conditional'' negation, and hence especially in connexion with the jussive ({{GHGpar|109|c}} and ''e'') to introduce prohibitions, warnings, negative desires, and requests. On {{GHGheb|text=אַל־}} with the imperfect, see {{GHGpar|107|p}}; with the cohortative, see {{GHGpar|108|c}}; on {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=6|verse=27}}, see {{GHGpar|109|h}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|152|g}}
Rem. 1. {{GHGheb|text=אַל־}} (like {{GHGheb|text=לֹא}}, see note on ''a'' above) may be used to form a compound word, as in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=12|verse=28}} {{GHGheb|text=אַל־מָוֶת|translate=not-death}} (immortality); though all the early versions read {{GHGheb|text=אֶל־מָוֶת}}. The instances in which {{GHGheb|text=אַל}} appears to stand absolutely, equivalent to ''no, certainly not'' (like μή for μὴ γένηται), e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ru|chapter=1|verse=13}} {{GHGheb|text=אַל בְּנֹתַי|translate=nay, my daughters}}, and {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=19|verse=18}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=33|verse=10|hidebook=1}} ({{GHGheb|text=אַל־נָא}}), are also due (see under ''c'') to extreme shortening of a full clause (in {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=13|verse=25}} such a clause is repeated immediately<section end="par152" /><noinclude>
